hints: Focus on what each reagent is really testing for, oxidation in the first case and the special iodoform group in the second.
Remember acidified dichromate(VI) oxidises primary and secondary alcohols and aldehydes, but it leaves ketones unchanged.

Recall only molecules containing $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ give a yellow precipitate with alkaline aqueous iodine, so look for the one structure that satisfies both tests.
walkthrough:
**What does acidified dichromate(VI) do?**

It is a strong oxidising agent that turns orange to green when it oxidises something. It oxidises primary alcohols to aldehydes then acids, secondary alcohols to ketones, and aldehydes to acids.

Rule:
$$\text{primary alcohol, secondary alcohol, aldehyde} \rightarrow \text{oxidised, ketone} \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Apply this to the four compounds**

Option A is a ketone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, so it resists further oxidation. Options B and D are alcohols and option C is an aldehyde, so B, C and D will all react with acidified dichromate(VI).

**What does alkaline aqueous iodine do?**

This is the iodoform test for the group $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. A positive result is a yellow precipitate of triiodomethane, $\text{CHI}_3$.

**Apply this to the shortlist**

Only B contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$, as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. It will first be oxidised and then give iodoform. That makes it the only compound that passes both tests.

options.A: Butan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, does give a positive iodoform test because it has $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$, but as a ketone it is not oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI). It fails the first test.
options.B: Butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a secondary alcohol so it is oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI) to butan-2-one. It also contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, so it gives a positive iodoform test with alkaline aqueous iodine. It passes both tests.
options.C: Butanal, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is an aldehyde so it is oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI), but it lacks $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. Only ethanal gives iodoform among aldehydes, so it fails the second test.
options.D: Butan-1-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, is a primary alcohol so it is oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI), but its OH is on carbon 1, not in a $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group. It therefore gives a negative iodoform test.
